question.text: What is the maximum period for which a rights issue can remain open under SEBI ICDR Regulations?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI (ICDR) framework for rights issues, the issue may remain open for a maximum of 30 working days. This longer cap is intended to give existing shareholders adequate time to review the offer, arrange funds, and submit applications. The Trap: "15 working days" is a commonly recalled older figure but no longer represents the current maximum. "21 working days" and "45 working days" are plausible-looking distractors that do not correspond to the prescribed ceiling. Note: The 30-working-day maximum open period for a rights issue is not stated on the cited NISM Series IX Merchant Banking workbook pages (which support a 3-to-10 working day window for IPOs and discuss rights-issue materials, record date, advertisements and closure without specifying a 30-day maximum). The 30-working-day figure above is referenced as general SEBI (ICDR) regulatory knowledge, not as a workbook-page citation.
